works.title: Time Transfixed (La durée poignardée)
works.note: Magritte painted this for the British patron Edward James, and it was the second picture delivered for James's ballroom in London. The French title means, literally, ongoing time stabbed by a dagger, and Magritte was reportedly unhappy with the English one. James sold it to the Art Institute of Chicago in 1970, when he was raising money for his sculpture garden, Las Pozas.

works.title: Birthday
works.note: Tanning painted this self-portrait in 1942, when she was thirty-one or thirty-two. As she recounts in her memoirs, Max Ernst saw it when he came to her studio to consider her work for an exhibition at Peggy Guggenheim's gallery in New York, and was enchanted by it. The two played chess, fell in love, and married in 1946. In 1986 she gave her first memoir the painting's title.

works.title: Waterfall
works.note: This lithograph was first printed in October 1961. The watercourse is built from three Penrose triangles, an impossible object designed by Oscar Reutersvärd in 1934 and found independently by Roger Penrose in 1958. The giant plants below the mill are a magnified view of a cluster of moss and lichen that Escher had drawn in ink in 1942. In his notes on the picture he pointed out that some water must be added now and then to make up for evaporation.
